bull.b: Starting a global Phase III trial materially advances pemvidutide toward a potential registrational outcome in MASH. The broad site footprint and defined enrollment plan demonstrate development execution and create an important long-term catalyst beyond the company’s current pre-commercial status.

The strengthened cash position and low leverage reduce near-term financing pressure while supporting the core MASH program through a major clinical milestone. This gives management greater flexibility to execute development plans without immediate reliance on additional equity financing for PERFORMA.

bull.t: Positive AUD Efficacy and Pipeline Breadth
bull.b: Positive Phase II AUD results expand pemvidutide’s potential beyond obesity and MASH into a large, undertreated liver-related indication. Multiple efficacy measures, including objective biomarkers and abstinence outcomes, support a differentiated development pathway and broaden future commercialization potential.

bear.b: Altimmune remains dependent on external capital because negligible product revenue does not offset substantial research and operating costs. Persistent losses and annual cash outflows in this range can consume shareholder capital over time and leave profitability contingent on successful clinical development.

bear.t: Funding Gap for Potential AUD Phase III
bear.b: A future AUD pivotal trial would require additional financing or a strategic transaction beyond the currently funded MASH plan. Management’s preference for royalties, debt, or partnerships may reduce dilution, but those sources are not guaranteed and could constrain timing or program scope.

Gastrointestinal discontinuations could limit dose persistence or complicate regulatory assessment if the pattern becomes material in later trials. At the same time, competition for MASH patients may increase enrollment costs and delay execution, weakening the speed of pemvidutide’s development.
